# Kigumi

> shadcn/ui for Web Awesome. Framework-specific component wrappers for React and Vue. Version 0.13.0.

Kigumi generates React and Vue wrapper components around Web Awesome web components. Components are copied into your project (not imported from a package), giving you full ownership and customization control.

Web Awesome's own llms.txt (at node_modules/@awesome.me/webawesome-pro/dist/llms.txt) documents the raw web component API. This file documents the Kigumi application layer: React/Vue wrapper APIs, composition patterns, layout utilities, state management, and accessibility guidance.

## Project Detection

A Kigumi project has a `kigumi.config.json` in the project root.

Read it to determine:
- `framework`: "react" or "vue"
- `typescript`: true or false
- `componentsDir`: where components live (default: "src/components/ui")
- `theme.selected`: active theme name
- `theme.palette`: color palette
- `theme.brandColor`: primary color

## CLI Introspection

Machine-readable project state:

```bash
npx kigumi status --json
```

Output schema:
```json
{
  "version": "0.13.0",
  "tier": "free",
  "framework": "react",
  "typescript": true,
  "componentsDir": "src/components/ui",
  "theme": { "selected": "awesome", "palette": "rudimentary", "brandColor": "blue" },
  "token": false,
  "package": { "package": "@awesome.me/webawesome", "version": "3.3.1" },
  "components": ["Button", "Card", "Dialog"],
  "warnings": []
}
```

List available components:
```bash
npx kigumi list --json
```

Output: array of `{ name, category, description }`.

Check installed components by listing subdirectories of `componentsDir`.

## Tier System

| Tier | Package | Detection |
|------|---------|-----------|
| Free | @awesome.me/webawesome | No token in .env |
| Pro  | @awesome.me/webawesome-pro | WEBAWESOME_NPM_TOKEN in .env |

Pro-only components: Page, Chart, BarChart, LineChart, BubbleChart, DoughnutChart, PieChart, PolarAreaChart, RadarChart, ScatterChart, Combobox, FileInput, NumberInput, Sparkline, Toast, ToastItem

## Critical Rules

1. Use `class` (not `className`) on web components and Kigumi wrapper components. `className` does not propagate through Shadow DOM.
2. Use `className` on standard HTML elements (`<div>`, `<form>`, `<section>`).
3. Form controls emit native DOM events (input, change, blur, focus). Read values via `e.target.value`. NOT CustomEvent.
4. Overlay components (Dialog, Drawer, Dropdown) emit custom `wa-*` events (wa-show, wa-hide). These ARE CustomEvent.
5. Use `requestClose()` not `hide()` on Dialog/Drawer refs. requestClose() triggers the wa-hide event lifecycle.
6. Never use `!important` in CSS. Use CSS cascade layers (base < theme) for specificity.
7. Always provide the `label` prop on Dialog, Drawer, Input, Select, Textarea for accessibility.

## Available Skills

For deeper AI-assisted workflows, install Kigumi agent skills:

- **kigumi-react**: Convert Web Awesome HTML to Kigumi React components
- **kigumi-vue**: Convert Web Awesome HTML to Kigumi Vue components
- **kigumi-theme**: Customize themes, CSS variables, design tokens, dark mode
- **kigumi-compose-form**: Build complete forms with validation and error handling
- **kigumi-compose-layout**: Build page layouts, dashboards, app shells
- **kigumi-compose-overlay**: Build modals, drawers, dropdown menus, toasts
- **kigumi-compose-data**: Build data tables, stats dashboards, list views

---

## Component Reference

All components available in the Kigumi registry, grouped by category. Each entry shows the Web Awesome tag, install command, import pattern, key props, slots, events, and CSS parts.

**Import convention:**

- React: `import { ComponentName } from '@/components/ui'`
- Vue: `import { ComponentName } from '@/components/ui'` (only where Vue templates exist)

---

### Actions

### Button

**Tag:** `wa-button` | **Category:** Actions | **Tier:** free
**Install:** `npx kigumi add button`
**React:** `import { Button } from '@/components/ui'`

**Key Props:** variant (neutral/brand/success/warning/danger), appearance (accent/filled-outlined/filled/outlined/plain), size (small/medium/large), pill (boolean), disabled (boolean), loading (boolean), with-caret (boolean), href (string), target (string), type (button/submit/reset)
**Slots:** (default), start, end
**React Events:** onBlur, onFocus, onWaInvalid
**CSS Parts:** base, start, label, end

### ButtonGroup

**Tag:** `wa-button-group` | **Category:** Actions | **Tier:** free
**Install:** `npx kigumi add button-group`
**React:** `import { ButtonGroup } from '@/components/ui'`

**Key Props:** label (string), orientation (horizontal/vertical)
**Slots:** (default)
**React Events:** (none)
**CSS Parts:** base

### CopyButton

**Tag:** `wa-copy-button` | **Category:** Actions | **Tier:** free
**Install:** `npx kigumi add copy-button`
**React:** `import { CopyButton } from '@/components/ui'`

**Key Props:** value (string), from (string), disabled (boolean), copy-label (string), success-label (string), error-label (string), feedback-duration (number), tooltip-placement (top/right/bottom/left)

**CSS Parts:** button, copy-icon, success-icon, error-icon

## Layout System

Kigumi includes CSS utility classes from Web Awesome for composing layouts without writing custom CSS. These are applied via `className` on standard HTML elements (NOT `class` on web components).

**IMPORTANT:** Use `className` on `<div>`, `<section>`, `<form>`, and other HTML elements. Use `class` on `<wa-*>` web components and Kigumi wrapper components (`<Button>`, `<Card>`, etc.).

### Layout Primitives

| Class | Purpose | Key Custom Property |
|-------|---------|-------------------|
| `.wa-stack` | Vertical stacking with consistent gap | -- |
| `.wa-grid` | Responsive auto-fit column grid | `--min-column-size` (default: 250px) |
| `.wa-cluster` | Horizontal wrapping group (tags, chips, buttons) | -- |
| `.wa-flank` | Sidebar + main content layout | `--flank-size` (default: 15rem) |
| `.wa-frame` | Aspect-ratio constrained container | -- |
| `.wa-split` | Two-column equal split | `--content-percentage` (default: 50%) |

### Gap Scale

| Class | Approximate Size |
|-------|-----------------|
| `.wa-gap-0` | 0 |
| `.wa-gap-3xs` | ~2px |
| `.wa-gap-2xs` | ~4px |
| `.wa-gap-xs` | ~8px |
| `.wa-gap-s` | ~12px |
| `.wa-gap-m` | ~16px |
| `.wa-gap-l` | ~24px |
| `.wa-gap-xl` | ~32px |
| `.wa-gap-2xl` | ~40px |
| `.wa-gap-3xl` | ~48px |

### Alignment Classes

**Align Items (cross axis):**
`.wa-align-items-start`, `.wa-align-items-center`, `.wa-align-items-end`, `.wa-align-items-stretch`, `.wa-align-items-baseline`

**Justify Content (main axis):**
`.wa-justify-content-start`, `.wa-justify-content-center`, `.wa-justify-content-end`, `.wa-justify-content-space-between`, `.wa-justify-content-space-around`, `.wa-justify-content-space-evenly`

### Custom Properties

Override layout behavior with CSS custom properties:

```css
/* Change grid minimum column width */
.my-grid {
  --min-column-size: 200px;
}

/* Change flank sidebar width */
.my-layout {
  --flank-size: 20rem;
}

/* Change split ratio */
.my-split {
  --content-percentage: 33%;
}
```

### Quick Example: Form Layout (React)

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Select, Option } from '@/components/ui';

function ContactForm() {
  return (
    <form>
      <div className="wa-stack wa-gap-m">
        <div className="wa-grid wa-gap-m" style={{ '--min-column-size': '200px' } as React.CSSProperties}>
          <Input label="First name" name="firstName" required />
          <Input label="Last name" name="lastName" required />
        </div>
        <Input label="Email" type="email" name="email" required />
        <Select label="Department" name="department">
          <Option value="engineering">Engineering</Option>
          <Option value="design">Design</Option>
          <Option value="product">Product</Option>
        </Select>
        <Button type="submit" variant="brand">Submit</Button>
      </div>
    </form>
  );
}
```

---

## Composition Patterns

Concrete code examples for common UI patterns in both React and Vue.

### 1. Form with Validation

**React:**

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Select, Option, Checkbox } from '@/components/ui';
import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';

function SignupForm() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);

  const handleSubmit = async (e: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    setLoading(true);
    const formData = new FormData(e.currentTarget);
    const data = Object.fromEntries(formData);
    await fetch('/api/signup', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) });
    setLoading(false);
  };

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <div className="wa-stack wa-gap-m">
        <Input
          label="Full name"
          name="name"
          required
          onInput={(e) => console.log(e.target.value)}
        />
        <Input label="Email" type="email" name="email" required />
        <Select label="Role" name="role" required>
          <Option value="developer">Developer</Option>
          <Option value="designer">Designer</Option>
        </Select>
        <Checkbox name="terms" required>
          I agree to the terms of service
        </Checkbox>
        <Button type="submit" variant="brand" loading={loading}>
          Create Account
        </Button>
      </div>
    </form>
  );
}
```

**Vue:**

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { Button, Input, Select, Option, Checkbox } from '@/components/ui';

const loading = ref(false);

async function handleSubmit(e: Event) {
  e.preventDefault();
  loading.value = true;
  const formData = new FormData(e.target as HTMLFormElement);
  const data = Object.fromEntries(formData);
  await fetch('/api/signup', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) });
  loading.value = false;
}
</script>

<template>
  <form @submit="handleSubmit">
    <div class="wa-stack wa-gap-m">
      <Input label="Full name" name="name" required />
      <Input label="Email" type="email" name="email" required />
      <Select label="Role" name="role" required>
        <Option value="developer">Developer</Option>
        <Option value="designer">Designer</Option>
      </Select>
      <Checkbox name="terms" required>
        I agree to the terms of service
      </Checkbox>
      <Button type="submit" variant="brand" :loading="loading">
        Create Account
      </Button>
    </div>
  </form>
</template>
```

### 2. Dialog with Form

**React:**

```tsx
import { Button, Dialog, Input } from '@/components/ui';
import { useState, useRef, useEffect } from 'react';

function EditProfileDialog() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = dialogRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const handleHide = () => setOpen(false);
    el.addEventListener('wa-after-hide', handleHide);
    return () => el.removeEventListener('wa-after-hide', handleHide);
  }, []);

  const handleSubmit = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    setLoading(true);
    await fetch('/api/profile', { method: 'PUT' });
    setLoading(false);
    dialogRef.current?.requestClose();
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Edit Profile</Button>
      <Dialog ref={dialogRef} label="Edit Profile" open={open}>
        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
          <div className="wa-stack wa-gap-m">
            <Input label="Display name" name="displayName" required />
            <Input label="Bio" name="bio" />
          </div>
        </form>
        <div slot="footer">
          <div className="wa-cluster wa-gap-s wa-justify-content-end">
            <Button appearance="outlined" onClick={() => dialogRef.current?.requestClose()}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button type="submit" variant="brand" loading={loading} onClick={handleSubmit}>
              Save
            </Button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

**Vue:**

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { Button, Dialog, Input } from '@/components/ui';

const open = ref(false);
const loading = ref(false);
const dialogEl = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null);

async function handleSubmit(e: Event) {
  e.preventDefault();
  loading.value = true;
  await fetch('/api/profile', { method: 'PUT' });
  loading.value = false;
  dialogEl.value?.requestClose();
}

function handleAfterHide() {
  open.value = false;
}
</script>

<template>
  <Button @click="open = true">Edit Profile</Button>
  <Dialog ref="dialogEl" label="Edit Profile" :open="open" @wa-after-hide="handleAfterHide">
    <form @submit="handleSubmit">
      <div class="wa-stack wa-gap-m">
        <Input label="Display name" name="displayName" required />
        <Input label="Bio" name="bio" />
      </div>
    </form>
    <template #footer>
      <div class="wa-cluster wa-gap-s wa-justify-content-end">
        <Button appearance="outlined" @click="dialogEl?.requestClose()">Cancel</Button>
        <Button type="submit" variant="brand" :loading="loading" @click="handleSubmit">Save</Button>
      </div>
    </template>
  </Dialog>
</template>
```

### 3. Dropdown Menu

**React:**

```tsx
import { Button, Dropdown, DropdownItem, Divider, Icon } from '@/components/ui';

function ActionsMenu() {
  return (
    <Dropdown>
      <Button slot="trigger" with-caret>Actions</Button>
      <DropdownItem>
        <Icon slot="icon" name="pen-to-square" />
        Edit
      </DropdownItem>
      <DropdownItem>
        <Icon slot="icon" name="copy" />
        Duplicate
      </DropdownItem>
      <Divider />
      <DropdownItem variant="danger">
        <Icon slot="icon" name="trash" />
        Delete
      </DropdownItem>
    </Dropdown>
  );
}
```

**Vue:**

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Button, Dropdown, DropdownItem, Divider, Icon } from '@/components/ui';
</script>

<template>
  <Dropdown>
    <Button slot="trigger" with-caret>Actions</Button>
    <DropdownItem>
      <Icon slot="icon" name="pen-to-square" />
      Edit
    </DropdownItem>
    <DropdownItem>
      <Icon slot="icon" name="copy" />
      Duplicate
    </DropdownItem>
    <Divider />
    <DropdownItem variant="danger">
      <Icon slot="icon" name="trash" />
      Delete
    </DropdownItem>
  </Dropdown>
</template>
```

### 5. Dashboard with Metrics

**React:**

```tsx
import { Card, FormatNumber, Icon, Badge } from '@/components/ui';

function Dashboard() {
  const metrics = [
    { label: 'Revenue', value: 48250, type: 'currency' as const, icon: 'dollar-sign', trend: 'up' },
    { label: 'Users', value: 12840, type: 'decimal' as const, icon: 'users', trend: 'up' },
    { label: 'Bounce Rate', value: 0.032, type: 'percent' as const, icon: 'arrow-trend-down', trend: 'down' },
    { label: 'Avg Session', value: 245, type: 'decimal' as const, icon: 'clock', trend: 'up' },
  ];

  return (
    <div className="wa-grid wa-gap-m" style={{ '--min-column-size': '220px' } as React.CSSProperties}>
      {metrics.map((m) => (
        <Card key={m.label}>
          <div className="wa-stack wa-gap-xs">
            <div className="wa-cluster wa-gap-s wa-align-items-center">
              <Icon name={m.icon} />
              <span>{m.label}</span>
            </div>
            <strong style={{ fontSize: 'var(--wa-font-size-2xl)' }}>
              <FormatNumber value={m.value} type={m.type} currency="USD" />
            </strong>
            <Badge variant={m.trend === 'up' ? 'success' : 'danger'} appearance="outlined" pill>
              <Icon slot="start" name={m.trend === 'up' ? 'arrow-up' : 'arrow-down'} />
              {m.trend === 'up' ? '+12%' : '-3%'}
            </Badge>
          </div>
        </Card>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

**Vue:**

### 7. Data Table with Status Badges

**React:**

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, Icon } from '@/components/ui';

const statusVariant = {
  active: 'success',
  pending: 'warning',
  inactive: 'danger',
} as const;

interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  role: string;
  status: keyof typeof statusVariant;
}

function UsersTable({ users }: { users: User[] }) {
  return (
    <table style={{ width: '100%', borderCollapse: 'collapse' }}>
      <thead>
        <tr style={{ borderBottom: 'var(--wa-border-width-s) solid var(--wa-color-neutral-border-quiet)' }}>
          <th style={{ textAlign: 'start', padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>Name</th>
          <th style={{ textAlign: 'start', padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>Email</th>
          <th style={{ textAlign: 'start', padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>Role</th>
          <th style={{ textAlign: 'start', padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>Status</th>
          <th style={{ textAlign: 'end', padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>Actions</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {users.map((user) => (
          <tr key={user.id} style={{ borderBottom: 'var(--wa-border-width-s) solid var(--wa-color-neutral-border-quiet)' }}>
            <td style={{ padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>{user.name}</td>
            <td style={{ padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>{user.email}</td>
            <td style={{ padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>{user.role}</td>
            <td style={{ padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)' }}>
              <Badge variant={statusVariant[user.status]} pill>{user.status}</Badge>
            </td>
            <td style={{ padding: 'var(--wa-space-s)', textAlign: 'end' }}>
              <Button size="small" appearance="outlined">
                <Icon slot="start" name="pen-to-square" /> Edit
              </Button>
            </td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}
```

**Vue:**

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Badge, Button, Icon } from '@/components/ui';

const statusVariant = { active: 'success', pending: 'warning', inactive: 'danger' } as const;

}>();

        <th style="text-align: start; padding: var(--wa-space-s)">Status</th>
        <th style="text-align: end; padding: var(--wa-space-s)">Actions</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
```

### 8. Toast Notifications (Pro)

**React:**

```tsx
import { Toast, ToastItem, Button } from '@/components/ui';
import { useRef } from 'react';

function ToastDemo() {
  const toastRef = useRef<HTMLElement & { create: (msg: string, opts: Record<string, unknown>) => void }>(null);

  const notify = (variant: string, message: string) => {
    toastRef.current?.create(message, { variant, duration: 4000 });
  };

  return (
    <>
      <div className="wa-cluster wa-gap-s">
        <Button variant="success" onClick={() => notify('success', 'Changes saved successfully.')}>
          Success
        </Button>
        <Button variant="danger" onClick={() => notify('danger', 'Something went wrong.')}>
          Error
        </Button>
        <Button variant="warning" onClick={() => notify('warning', 'Disk space running low.')}>
          Warning
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Toast ref={toastRef} placement="top-end" />
    </>
  );
}
```

**Vue:**

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { Toast, Button } from '@/components/ui';

const toastEl = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null);

function notify(variant: string, message: string) {
  (toastEl.value as any)?.create(message, { variant, duration: 4000 });
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="wa-cluster wa-gap-s">
    <Button variant="success" @click="notify('success', 'Changes saved successfully.')">Success</Button>
    <Button variant="danger" @click="notify('danger', 'Something went wrong.')">Error</Button>
    <Button variant="warning" @click="notify('warning', 'Disk space running low.')">Warning</Button>
  </div>
  <Toast ref="toastEl" placement="top-end" />
</template>
```

---

## State Patterns

### Two Event Systems

Web Awesome components use two distinct event systems. Getting this wrong is the most common source of bugs.

| Category | Event Origin | Event Names | How to Read Value |
|----------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|
| Form controls (Input, Select, Checkbox, Textarea, Slider, Switch, Radio, Rating, ColorPicker, Combobox, NumberInput, FileInput) | Native DOM | input, change, blur, focus | `e.target.value` or `e.target.checked` |
| Overlays (Dialog, Drawer, Dropdown, Tooltip, Popover, Details) | CustomEvent | wa-show, wa-hide, wa-after-show, wa-after-hide | `e.detail` (varies) |
| Selection (Dropdown, Tree) | CustomEvent | wa-select, wa-selection-change | `e.detail.item` |
| Validation | CustomEvent | wa-invalid | `e.detail` |

### Controlled Overlay Pattern

**React:**

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);

// Open
<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open</Button>

// Sync close state via event
useEffect(() => {
  const el = dialogRef.current;
  if (!el) return;
  const handleHide = () => setOpen(false);
  el.addEventListener('wa-after-hide', handleHide);
  return () => el.removeEventListener('wa-after-hide', handleHide);
}, []);

// Close programmatically
dialogRef.current?.requestClose();
```

**Vue:**

```vue
const open = ref(false);
const dialogEl = ref(null);

// Open
<Button @click="open = true">Open</Button>

// Sync close
<Dialog :open="open" @wa-after-hide="open = false">

// Close programmatically
dialogEl.value?.requestClose();
```

### requestClose() vs hide()

Always use `requestClose()` on Dialog and Drawer. It triggers the `wa-hide` event lifecycle, which can be prevented with `event.preventDefault()`. Using `hide()` directly bypasses this lifecycle and breaks controlled state.

### Event Cleanup in useEffect

Every `addEventListener` in a `useEffect` MUST return a cleanup function:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const el = ref.current;
  if (!el) return;
  const handler = (e: Event) => { /* ... */ };
  el.addEventListener('wa-show', handler);
  return () => el.removeEventListener('wa-show', handler);
}, []);
```

### Form Input Value Reading

**React:**

```tsx
// Input, Textarea
<Input onInput={(e) => setValue((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} />

// Checkbox, Switch
<Checkbox onChange={(e) => setChecked((e.target as HTMLInputElement).checked)} />

// Select (single)
<Select onChange={(e) => setRole((e.target as HTMLSelectElement).value)}>

// Rating
<Rating onChange={(e) => setRating((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} />
```

**Vue:**

```vue
<!-- Input, Textarea -->
<Input @input="(e) => value = e.target.value" />

<!-- Checkbox, Switch -->
<Checkbox @change="(e) => checked = e.target.checked" />

<!-- Select (single) -->
<Select @change="(e) => role = e.target.value">
```

---

## Styling API

### CSS Cascade Layers

Kigumi uses CSS `@layer` for specificity management. The layer order is:

```
base < theme
```

- **base**: Web Awesome default styles
- **theme**: Your project's `theme.css` overrides

This means theme styles always override base styles without needing `!important`. NEVER use `!important` in Kigumi projects.

### CSS Parts

Style Shadow DOM internals using the `::part()` selector:

```css
/* Style the dialog body */
wa-dialog::part(body) {
  padding: var(--wa-space-xl);
}

/* Style button label */
wa-button::part(label) {
  font-weight: var(--wa-font-weight-bold);
}

/* Style input base */
wa-input::part(base) {
  border-radius: var(--wa-border-radius-l);
}
```

Each component's CSS Parts are listed in the Component Reference above.

### Design Tokens

Web Awesome provides semantic design tokens as CSS custom properties with the `--wa-` prefix. Override them at `:root` scope or on specific selectors.

**Color tokens:**
- `--wa-color-brand-fill-loud` / `--wa-color-brand-fill-normal` / `--wa-color-brand-fill-quiet`
- `--wa-color-neutral-fill-loud` / `--wa-color-neutral-fill-normal` / `--wa-color-neutral-fill-quiet`
- `--wa-color-success-fill-loud` / `--wa-color-success-fill-normal`
- `--wa-color-warning-fill-loud` / `--wa-color-warning-fill-normal`
- `--wa-color-danger-fill-loud` / `--wa-color-danger-fill-normal`
- `--wa-color-surface-default` / `--wa-color-surface-raised` / `--wa-color-surface-overlay`
- `--wa-color-surface-text` / `--wa-color-surface-text-quiet`
- `--wa-color-surface-border` / `--wa-color-neutral-border-quiet`

**Typography tokens:**
- `--wa-font-size-xs` through `--wa-font-size-3xl`
- `--wa-font-weight-light` / `--wa-font-weight-normal` / `--wa-font-weight-semibold` / `--wa-font-weight-bold`
- `--wa-line-height-dense` / `--wa-line-height-normal` / `--wa-line-height-loose`
- `--wa-font-family-sans` / `--wa-font-family-serif` / `--wa-font-family-mono`

**Spacing tokens:**
- `--wa-space-3xs` through `--wa-space-3xl`

**Border tokens:**
- `--wa-border-radius-s` / `--wa-border-radius-m` / `--wa-border-radius-l` / `--wa-border-radius-xl` / `--wa-border-radius-circle` / `--wa-border-radius-pill`
- `--wa-border-width-s` / `--wa-border-width-m` / `--wa-border-width-l`

**Shadow tokens:**
- `--wa-shadow-xs` through `--wa-shadow-xl`

**Transition tokens:**
- `--wa-transition-x-slow` / `--wa-transition-slow` / `--wa-transition-medium` / `--wa-transition-fast` / `--wa-transition-x-fast`

**Z-index tokens:**
- `--wa-z-index-drawer` / `--wa-z-index-dialog` / `--wa-z-index-dropdown` / `--wa-z-index-toast` / `--wa-z-index-tooltip`

### Override Pattern

Override tokens at `:root` for global changes, or on specific selectors for scoped changes:

```css
/* Global overrides in theme.css */
:root {
  --wa-color-brand-fill-loud: #6366f1;
  --wa-border-radius-m: 0.5rem;
  --wa-font-family-sans: 'Inter', sans-serif;
}

/* Dark mode overrides */
.wa-dark {
  --wa-color-surface-default: #1e1e2e;
  --wa-color-surface-text: #cdd6f4;
}
```

### Theme Configuration

Theme settings in `kigumi.config.json`:

```json
{
  "theme": {
    "selected": "awesome",
    "palette": "rudimentary",
    "brandColor": "blue"
  }
}
```

- `theme.selected`: The active theme preset (awesome, tailspin, poppins, etc.)
- `theme.palette`: Color palette (rudimentary, vivid, etc.)
- `theme.brandColor`: Primary brand color (blue, purple, red, green, etc.)

Change themes via CLI:

```bash
npx kigumi theme awesome       # Set theme
npx kigumi palette vivid       # Set palette
npx kigumi brand purple        # Set brand color
```

---

## Accessibility

### Form Controls

- **Always provide `label`**: Every Input, Select, Textarea, Slider, RadioGroup, Checkbox, Switch, ColorPicker, Combobox, NumberInput, and FileInput must have a `label` prop for screen readers.
- **Use `hint` for descriptions**: Add the `hint` prop to provide additional context beyond the label.
- **Required fields**: Set `required` prop. Web Awesome handles `aria-required` automatically.
- **Validation messages**: Use `setCustomValidity()` for custom error messages. The `wa-invalid` event fires when validation fails.

### Overlays

- **Always provide `label`**: Dialog and Drawer must have a `label` prop that describes their purpose.
- **Focus trap**: Dialog and Drawer automatically trap focus inside the overlay when open.
- **Escape to close**: Dialog and Drawer close on Escape key by default. Prevent this by calling `event.preventDefault()` on `wa-hide`.
- **Light dismiss**: Set `light-dismiss` to allow closing by clicking outside. Disabled by default for Dialog.

### Keyboard Navigation

Built-in keyboard support:
- **TabGroup**: Arrow keys navigate between tabs, Enter/Space activates
- **Tree**: Arrow keys navigate, Enter/Space selects, Left/Right expands/collapses
- **RadioGroup**: Arrow keys move between options
- **Dropdown**: Arrow keys navigate items, Enter/Space selects, Escape closes
- **Select**: Arrow keys navigate options, Enter/Space selects
- **Slider**: Arrow keys adjust value, Home/End for min/max

### Color

- Never rely on color alone to convey information. Always pair color with text, icons, or patterns.
- Badge variants (success, warning, danger) include both color and text content.
- Use sufficient color contrast. Web Awesome tokens are designed to meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards.

### Icons

- **Icon-only buttons**: Always add `aria-label` to buttons that contain only an icon:

```tsx
<Button aria-label="Delete item">
  <Icon name="trash" />
</Button>
```

- **Decorative icons**: Icons next to text labels are decorative and do not need labels. Web Awesome handles this automatically.

---

## CLI Reference

### npx kigumi init

Initialize a Kigumi project in the current directory.

```bash
npx kigumi init [options]
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--framework <name>` | Framework (react, vue) |
| `--theme <name>` | Theme preset |
| `--palette <name>` | Color palette |
| `--brand <color>` | Brand color |
| `--typescript` / `--no-typescript` | TypeScript support |
| `--components-dir <path>` | Component output directory |
| `--yes` | Skip prompts, use defaults |

### npx kigumi add

Add components to your project.

```bash
npx kigumi add <component...> [options]
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--overwrite` | Overwrite existing components |
| `--from <registry>` | Install from community registry |
| `--all` | Add all available components |

Examples:
```bash
npx kigumi add button card dialog
npx kigumi add button --overwrite
npx kigumi add --all
npx kigumi add custom-card --from my-registry
```

### npx kigumi list

List all available components.

```bash
npx kigumi list [options]
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--json` | Machine-readable JSON output |
| `--category <name>` | Filter by category |

### npx kigumi status

Show project status and configuration.

```bash
npx kigumi status [options]
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--json` | Machine-readable JSON output |

### npx kigumi theme

Set the active theme.

```bash
npx kigumi theme <name>
npx kigumi theme list
npx kigumi theme show
npx kigumi theme install --from <registry>
```

### npx kigumi brand

Set the brand color.

```bash
npx kigumi brand <color>
```

### npx kigumi palette

Set the color palette.

```bash
npx kigumi palette <name>
```

### npx kigumi doctor

Diagnose common issues (imports, tier, config).

```bash
npx kigumi doctor
```

### npx kigumi diff

Compare installed components against current templates to see what changed.

```bash
npx kigumi diff [component...]
```

### npx kigumi update

Update installed components using three-way merge (preserves your edits).

```bash
npx kigumi update [component...] [options]
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--force` | Overwrite without merge |
| `--dry-run` | Preview changes without writing |

### npx kigumi upgrade

Check for and apply CLI version upgrades.

```bash
npx kigumi upgrade
```

### npx kigumi registry

Manage community component registries.

```bash
npx kigumi registry connect <name> <url>
npx kigumi registry list
npx kigumi registry remove <name>
```
